experiment: E1: hand-set energies, no learned parameters, no training

rows.flop_convention: cram_sudoku_sparse.SparseSearch, as cram-l1-sparse: per move per chain 4 D (two neighbour-field updates) + (D + 1) (focus) + (2 d + 1) (heat bath without input costs) + 4 (energy and test) = 124 flop at D = 20, d = 9; a multiply-add is 2 flop; index, comparison and RNG operations 0; a puzzle pays all 4 chains up to its stop
rows.test_set: Sudoku-Extreme official test less dev10k: full-all rows 10,000-422,785 (412,786 puzzles), x 3 inference seeds

rows.flop_convention: maze_unique.gibbs_flop, as cram-fg: one full current (2 x 2 x 2 x 9 x 900 = 64,800 flop) plus per move 4 x 8 (the field change at the 8 neighbours) + 2 x 900 (focus); a multiply-add is 2 flop

hand_justification.Fp, Gp = (0.1, 1, 0.1): the kernel is 2 K F[dr] G[dc]: side neighbours get 2 x 0.1 x 1 = 0.2, diagonal ones 0.02, so diagonals weigh 1/10 of a side; a rank-1 offset product cannot make them exactly 0
hand_justification.K(on, on) = Q P^T = -5: scales the side coupling to -1 per on side neighbour and the diagonal one to -0.1; K = 0 for any off state, so walls and removed cells exert no field
hand_justification.b = (0, -1.5): an on open cell pays 1.5: it stays on iff (on sides) + 0.1 (on diagonals) > 1.5, which holds for 2 on sides and fails for at most 1 (1 + 0.1 x 4 = 1.4 < 1.5), with no ties
hand_justification.P, Q other entries = 0: no coupling involves the off state, and the second factor column is unused

rows.test_set: EqR maze-30x30-unique-1k test (1,000 mazes), x 3 inference seeds
